note: 47 of the 113 columns in BTS1_BTS2_fields_preserved.csv. THIS IS THE WIDE EXPORT AND THE MODEL WAS FITTED ON Combined.csv (52 columns) UNTIL ROUND 50; the two carry the same 1,215,890 rows, and the six columns the narrow one lacks are the difference between accuracy 0.76 and 0.98. One of them does all of it: `idle_time_ablation` in models/metrics.json refits without `IdleTime` alone every run and lands on the old score. The 66 dropped columns are listed above WITH THE REASON each was dropped. They are 3 targets, 9 row identifiers, 10 host fingerprints, 5 columns bit-identical to `Dur`, and 39 that hold exactly one state in this release - 30 of those are 100% null, including every SIntPkt/DIntPkt inter-packet-time and jitter column, which are EMPTY here and not merely uninformative. `Unnamed: 0` IS THE ONE TO CHECK FIRST. It is the CSV's own row index and leaving it in takes accuracy to 0.9997, which is the range published for this corpus and is a leak rather than a result; `leak_counterfactual_*` in models/metrics.json re-measures it every run. A SEPARATE AND LEGITIMATE MATTER, stated because the numbers look alarming next to that: 24 of the 47 kept features still clear the 0.90 one-vs-rest AUC threshold after all 66 drops. Those are real flow statistics rather than bookkeeping columns: each attack class in this corpus was produced by a different tool against a different service, so packet rate, ACK timing, TTL and TCP window separating them is the signal an intrusion detector is meant to use. They are reported and kept. The row identifiers cleared the same threshold while describing only where a row sits in a file, and that is the distinction this file exists to make - see `single_feature_leak_check` in models/metrics.json for the full measured list. `categorical_vocabularies` is the ordinal encoding the ten string columns were fitted under; index into the list, and use `missing_value` for anything absent or unseen. THE LEADING AND TRAILING SPACES IN `Flgs`, `Dir` AND `TcpOpt` ARE PART OF THE VALUE: Argus writes them as fixed-width fields and the vocabulary is the raw cell, so look up the cell as read and do not strip it. The vocabulary is published rather than re-derived because one rebuilt from different rows would remap codes the ONNX thresholds were fitted against.
